title: Bài 2: Cuộc Đời Đa-vít
subtitle: The Life of David — 1 Samuel 16-17; Psalm 51 · Ngữ pháp: Past perfect (had + past participle); past perfect vs past simple in narrative
grammar_topic: Past perfect (had + past participle); past perfect vs past simple in narrative
pronunciation_detail: Why it matters: In natural English, words do not stand alone — they link together in a smooth stream. Vietnamese speakers often pronounce each word separately, with a small pause between words, so their English sounds slow and choppy. Linking makes you sound natural and helps you understand native speakers, who almost never pause between words. Linking /r/ — When a word ends in the letter r (or the sound /r/) and the next word begins with a vowel, the /r/ links across: “fear‿of God” (/fɪər əv ɡɒd/), “far‿away”, “law‿and order” (the /r/ in “law” is a linking /r/ in British English). Do not stop after “fear” — glide straight into “of”. Linking /w/ — When a word ends in a /uː/ or /əʊ/ sound (like go, how, do) and the next word begins with a vowel, a small /w/ glides between them: “go‿out” (/ɡəʊ‿waʊt/), “how‿old”, “do‿it”. Your lips round for the /w/ — feel them move! Weak “and”: In phrases like “David and Goliath”, “and” is weak — /ən/, not /ænd/. Say the whole name as one phrase: “David‿ən‿Goliath”. Practice: read each phrase in Exercise 4 aloud three times, faster each time, until the words join into one smooth sound.
objectives: Học và thực hành: Past perfect (had + past participle); past perfect vs past simple in narrative.
Luyện phát âm: Connected speech: linking /r/ and /w/.

grammar.title: Past perfect (had + past participle); past perfect vs past simple in narrative
grammar.explain:
Form: had + past participle — had chosen, had waited, had already looked, had given. The past perfect describes the earlier of two past actions. Think of a timeline: the past perfect is the action that happened first, further back in the past; the past simple is the action that happened second, closer to now.

Structure 1: “By the time + past simple, … had + past participle” “By the time Samuel arrived, Jesse had already presented seven sons.” — Samuel’s arrival is the later past moment; Jesse’s presenting happened before it. “By the time Goliath fell, David had thrown only one stone.” Use already before the participle to stress that the earlier action was complete: had already chosen, had already promised.

Structure 2: “After / Before” with two past actions “David repented after Nathan had told him the truth.” (Nathan’s telling came first.) “Samuel anointed David after God had rejected Saul.” With after, the past perfect follows it; with before, the past perfect comes first: “Before David became king, he had looked after his father’s sheep for many years.”

Structure 3: Past perfect vs. past simple — don’t mix them up Past simple = a finished action in the past: “David killed Goliath.” Past perfect = an action finished before another past action: “David had killed a lion and a bear before he fought Goliath.” In a story, use the past simple for the main events and the past perfect only to “step back” and explain what had happened earlier. If you use the past perfect for everything, your story sounds wrong — use it like a flashback, not like the main plot. Common mistakes: (1) Forgetting had: “God chosen David” — wrong; say “God had chosen David.” (2) Past perfect for a single past event: “David had killed Goliath yesterday” — wrong; say “David killed Goliath.” (3) Base verb after had: “had choose” — wrong; say “had chosen.”

reading_passage: David was the youngest of Jesse’s eight sons, and nobody expected him to become king. While his older brothers joined King Saul’s army, David stayed home and looked after his father’s sheep. It taught him two things: how to fight wild animals, and how to trust God. When a lion or a bear attacked the flock, David fought it and saved the sheep. One day, the prophet Samuel came to Bethlehem. God had told Samuel to anoint a new king, and Samuel had already looked at David’s seven older brothers. But God said, “Man looks on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.” So Samuel sent for David and anointed him king of Israel. God had chosen the youngest son, the one with a humble and faithful heart. Later, Israel faced the Philistines, whose champion was a giant named Goliath. For forty days, Goliath had shouted his challenge, and no soldier in Israel had dared to fight him. Then David arrived, and he heard the giant’s voice. “I will fight him,” David said. He refused Saul’s heavy armour — it was too big for him — and took his sling and five smooth stones from the stream, ran toward Goliath, and struck him down with one stone. The battle belonged to the LORD. But David was not perfect. Years later, he sinned against God and Uriah, and tried to hide his sin. God sent Nathan, and David repented. He prayed the words of Psalm 51: “Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.” David was called “a man after God’s own heart” — not because he never sinned, but because he always came back to God in repentance and trusted in His mercy.

reading_comprehension.q: 1. What two things did David’s job as a shepherd teach him?
reading_comprehension.a: How to fight wild animals, and how to trust God.

reading_comprehension.q: 2. Why did God choose David instead of his older brothers?
reading_comprehension.a: God looks on the heart, not on outward appearance; David had a humble and faithful heart.

reading_comprehension.q: 3. Why did David refuse to wear Saul’s armour?
reading_comprehension.a: Saul’s armour was too big for him, so he refused to wear it.

reading_comprehension.q: 4. What does the passage say was the reason David was called “a man after God’s own heart”?
reading_comprehension.a: Not because he never sinned, but because he always came back to God in repentance and trusted in His mercy.

listening_questions.q: 1. True or False: David was the oldest of Jesse's sons.
listening_questions.a: False. David was the youngest of eight sons.

listening_questions.q: 2. True or False: Samuel had already looked at David's seven older brothers before God chose David.
3. How long had Goliath shouted his challenge before David fought him?
4. What did David use to defeat Goliath?
listening_questions.a: A sling and one smooth stone.

listening_questions.q: 5. What did David pray in Psalm 51?
listening_questions.a: "Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me."

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Past Perfect or Past Simple?
exercises.instruction: Choose the correct verb form. Remember: the past perfect (had + past participle) describes the EARLIER of two past actions.

exercises.title: Exercise 2: Complete the Story — Past Perfect and Past Simple
exercises.instruction: Put each verb in brackets into the past perfect (had + past participle) or the past simple.

exercises.title: Exercise 3: Vocabulary Matching
exercises.instruction: Match each word with its correct definition.

exercises.title: Exercise 4: Connected Speech — Linking /r/ and /w/
exercises.instruction: In connected speech, a word ending in /r/ or /w/ links smoothly to the next word beginning with a vowel. Read each phrase aloud as ONE smooth sound, without a pause. Then underline the linking sound.

exercises.title: Exercise 5: Ministry Translation Lab (Vietnamese to English)
exercises.instruction: Translate into natural English. Use the past perfect where the Vietnamese shows one past action happened before another.

exercises.title: Exercise 6: Guided Ministry Writing (80-100 words)
exercises.instruction: Retell the story of David and Goliath in your own words (80-100 words). Use the past perfect at least THREE times, and use at least 4 target words (shepherd, giant, sling, courage, faith, victory).

speaking_task: In pairs (10 minutes): Student A retells the anointing of David (1 Samuel 16) in your own words; Student B retells David and Goliath (1 Samuel 17). Each story must use the past perfect at least 3 times (“By the time…, …had already…”). Then discuss together: “Why was David called ‘a man after God’s own heart’?” Use linking /r/ and /w/ in your answers (“fear of God”, “go out”, “David and Goliath”).

written.q: 1. By the time David fought Goliath, he __________ (already / save) his sheep from a lion and a bear.
2. Samuel __________ (anoint) David after Jesse __________ (present) his seven older sons.

written.a: did not wear; had never tried
written.q: 3. David __________ (not wear) Saul's armour because he __________ (never / try) it in battle before.

written.a: "Before David became king, he had looked after his father's sheep for many years."
written.q: 4. Translate: Trước khi Đa-vít trở thành vua, ông đã chăn chiên cho cha mình nhiều năm.

written.a: "David repented because he knew that only God could give him a clean heart."
written.q: 5. Translate: Đa-vít đã ăn năn vì ông biết rằng chỉ Đức Chúa Trời mới có thể ban cho ông một tấm lòng trong sạch.

listening.a: Because God looks at the heart, not at outward appearance (1 Sam 16:7); David had a humble, faithful heart.
listening.q: 1. Why did God choose David, the youngest son, and not one of his older brothers?
2. What two animals had David already saved his sheep from before he faced Goliath?

listening.a: Not because David never sinned, but because he repented and trusted in God's mercy.
listening.q: 3. In the dialogue, what does the Friend learn about why David was called 'a man after God's own heart'?
